summary: Neo finds himself in a blank-white space that Morpheus calls the Construct, a loading program where anything can be loaded. Morpheus materializes beside him, demonstrates that Neo's appearance has changed (different clothes, vanished plugs, hair grown back) as 'residual self image,' and leads him to two leather chairs before a large television. When Neo asks if they are inside a computer program, Morpheus argues that what feels real is only electrical signals interpreted by the brain, then switches on the TV to show the Twentieth Century city Neo knew, explaining it now exists only as the Matrix, a neural-interactive simulation. He changes the channel to reveal the ruined present world, then descends with Neo through the screen to the scorched lake bed below. There Morpheus recounts how mankind, in hubris, created A.I., an artificial intelligence that spawned a race of machines; how war followed and humans scorched the sky believing the solar-powered machines would die; and how, ironically, humans remain dependent on machines to survive.

what_changes.before: believes he is in an ordinary room and questions the situation
what_changes.after: is shown that the world he knew is a simulation called the Matrix and that reality is a scorched wasteland
what_changes.evidence: You have been living inside a dreamworld, Neo. As in Baudrillard's vision, your whole life has been spent inside the map, not the territory.

what_changes.before: Startled, Neo whips around and finds Morpheus now in the room with him.
what_changes.after: We TURN AND DESCEND, SPIRALING DOWN TOWARD the lake bed ... where we FIND Morpheus and Neo. Neo clings to the chair, trying to get his bearings.
what_changes.evidence: We TURN AND DESCEND, SPIRALING DOWN TOWARD the lake bed which is scorched and split like burnt flesh, where we FIND Morpheus and Neo. Neo clings to the chair, trying to get his bearings.

what_changes.before: assumes the world is real and questions whether they are inside a computer program
what_changes.after: understands that reality is only electrical signals and that his body's image here is a mental projection
what_changes.evidence: It's what we call residual self image. The mental projection of your electronic self. Wild, isn't it?

event_hint.kind: a revelation / guided tour of the truth
event_hint.one_line: Morpheus brings Neo into the Construct and reveals the true nature of the Matrix and the scorched real world, explaining the origin of the war with the machines.

objects_that_matter: the two leather chairs from the Hotel Lafayette
uncertain: What Neo will choose to do with this knowledge
What happens next after the history lesson ends

minds.wants: To pin down what is real — a fixed point — so the vertigo of everything being programmable stops.
minds.feels: Terrified and unmoored; his senses keep reporting a solid world (leather, hair, a room) while every authority figure and his own body contradict it. The panic is physical — he clings to the chair, touches his head, runs his hands over the leather as if touch could settle the argument.
minds.shows: A stuttering, literal-minded skeptic ('This — This isn't real?', 'A.I.? You mean artificial intelligence?') who keeps asking for definitions and confirmations rather than absorbing the spectacle.
minds.basis: He whips around startled; touches his head when told his hair changed; grips the cracked leather and the chair; repeatedly reframes Morpheus's grand statements into plain questions ('Right now, we're inside a computer program?').

minds.wants: To keep Morpheus as a reliable guide even as Morpheus dismantles the only world Neo has ever trusted.
minds.feels: A dawning, uneasy dependence — he has no frame of reference left, so the man doing the explaining becomes the only furniture that isn't moving.
minds.shows: Compliance: he sits when told, follows the gaze to the screen, descends with him. His resistance is verbal/questioning, never physical refusal.
minds.basis: In sc-038–039 he followed Morpheus 'like a sleepwalker' and allowed himself to be wired in; here he obeys 'Sit down' and lets Morpheus lead him through the screen despite fear.

minds.wants: To break Neo's faith in the Matrix cleanly and completely, replacing it with faith in himself as the one who can show the truth.
minds.feels: Controlled, almost relishing. He is not anxious about the revelation; he is savoring it — the theatricality (remote, channel-change, descent, the sunglasses reflecting the storm) is a man who has done this and takes a grim aesthetic pleasure in it.
minds.shows: A calm, didactic showman who smiles at Neo's disbelief and answers questions with more questions ('What is real?'), staging the truth as spectacle rather than lecture.
minds.basis: He smiles at 'Is it so hard to believe?'; he choreographs the TV/channel/descend sequence; he lingers on irony ('almost funny', 'Fate, it seems, is not without a sense of irony').

minds.wants: To position Neo not as a random rescued prisoner but as someone worth the exception — the beginning of a special investment.
minds.feels: A quiet, private certainty beneath the exposition: he is watching the person he has been waiting for, though he is not yet ready to name it.
minds.shows: Nothing explicit here — he gives Neo the standard history-and-revelation treatment. The specialness is in what he withholds.
minds.basis: He personally guides Neo and says 'your whole life' with emphasis; ev-010 will reveal he broke a rule freeing older minds, implying this care is already selective.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the right mind to free and is worth breaking the rule for — that he can handle this truth and what it means.
believes_about.wrong_because: The next event has Neo's mind rejecting the overload and needing to be revived; Morpheus's confidence in Neo's readiness is, in the immediate term, already outrunning the reality.

minds.wants: To keep Neo from bolting for the comforting lie by making the truth feel like a relief rather than a threat.
minds.feels: A strategist's patience; he knows the revelation could shatter Neo, so he paces it — definition of 'real' first, then the city, then the wasteland, then the deep history — a graduated dose.
minds.shows: Rhetorical gentleness ('Is it so hard to believe?') and self-deprecating irony, which soften the blow of telling a man his entire life is a lie.
minds.basis: The ordered escalation of the demonstration and the soothing, conversational tone despite apocalyptic content; ev-009 confirms the dose is calibrated enough to nearly break him.

connects_back: sc-037: Neo's discovery of his grafted ports and regrown hair is the bodily proof Morpheus now names ('residual self image') and weaponizes as the first crack in Neo's sense of real.
sc-038–039: Neo's sleepwalker-trust and his being plugged into the Core is what makes this Construct demonstration possible and explains his compliance here.
sc-039: Morpheus's promise — 'There is no reason for me to try to explain it when I can simply show it' — is exactly the method executed in this scene.
The 'What is the Matrix?' question that has driven the whole arc is finally answered, paying off Neo's (and the audience's) long-standing ignorance.
sets_up: ev-009: Having established the simulation and the wasteland, Morpheus can now deliver the final, body-horror revelation (fetus fields, humans as batteries) that overwhelms Neo and makes him vomit/reject.
ev-010: Morpheus's claim that Neo 'cannot return' and his apology for freeing an older mind grows directly out of the bond and the selective investment seeded here.

ev-012–014: The Construct's rule that 'we can load anything' — weapons, training simulations — is the mechanism that will later let Neo download jujitsu, fight in the dojo, and attempt the rooftop jump.

Neo's new working model — 'real is electrical signals' and his body-image is a projection — is the conceptual foundation he will have to un-learn/rewrite in training ('There is no spoon' logic of the Matrix).
dramatic_function: This is the revelation scene that converts the story from mystery into mission: it swaps Neo's (and the audience's) ignorance for a complete new cosmology — simulation, ruined reality, and the origin of the machine war — while binding Neo's trust to Morpheus as guide, so that everything after is built on a truth he has been shown but has not yet been able to bear.
